final_scope.name: Step repetition
final_scope.rationale: Selected for practical importance and testability, not frequency. Repeated no-progress calls waste cost and can block completion, and a deliberately faulty tool makes the failure reproducible and directly measurable from tool-call logs.
final_scope.supporting_evidence: Model predictions: 4.6% of valid model responses (16.9% including rejected outputs); the summaries may be affected by the duplicate-quote validator defect found in Step 7. Step 7 disagreement ('List all my notes' / 'List all notes') shows the retry boundary a guard must respect.
final_scope.contrary_evidence: Rare in the human sample (1/17 eligible human traces) and one positive (langgraph-5062) among the 17 team-reviewed GitHub cases. It is not claimed to be the most common failure.
final_scope.uncertainty: Valid-only and all-output summaries are sensitivity analyses, not bounds on true prevalence. The GitHub positive is a reported case, not an independent reproduction. A live-agent pilot must check whether repetition arises naturally.
final_scope.candidate_pattern: Chain of Responsibility guard chain (identity, retry budget, state progress) with State-based recovery
final_scope.remediation_target: Detect three consecutive calls with the same normalized tool and arguments and no new information or state progress; route to recovery or an explicit failure; allow retries that make progress.
final_scope.testable_claim: Under a persistent tool fault, the guarded agent produces fewer repetition events than the baseline, without lowering task success under a transient fault.

definitions.step_repetition: Unnecessary reiteration of previously completed steps in a process, potentially causing delays or errors in task completion.

final_scope.name: Termination lifecycle (missed and premature termination)
final_scope.rationale: Both categories are two sides of one missing completion criterion: continuing after the task is done, or stopping before it is done. Both arise when termination is a token or flag instead of an explicit state.
final_scope.supporting_evidence: Human sample: unaware of termination in 4/17 eligible human traces. Model predictions: unaware 3.4% of valid model responses (12.3% including rejected outputs); premature 5.4% of valid model responses (6.9% including rejected outputs). Abstentions concentrate in these two categories, showing implicit completion criteria. GitHub: autogen-6746 carries a TERMINATE state into the next task (design smell).
final_scope.contrary_evidence: Premature termination has 0/4 eligible human traces positive. The team review rejected autogen-7043 because early completion alone does not show an ill-specified condition. Simon similarly records autogen-6710 as insufficient_evidence; a framework activation-counter bug alone does not establish the agent-behavior category.
final_scope.uncertainty: Few eligible human traces for premature termination, and category definitions changed between annotation rounds.
final_scope.candidate_pattern: State pattern: Running, Recovering, Completed, Failed
final_scope.remediation_target: Allow the transition to Completed only when task-specific postconditions hold; exhausting the budget moves to Failed with a reason instead of claiming success.
final_scope.testable_claim: In matched scenarios, the State-based controller never reports Completed when postconditions fail and never continues after they hold.

definitions.unaware_of_termination_conditions: Lack of recognition or understanding of the criteria that should trigger the termination of the agents’ interaction, potentially leading to unnecessary continuation.
definitions.premature_termination: Ill specified termination condition leading to premature termination Ending a dialogue, interaction or task before all necessary information has been exchanged or objectives have been met. Necessary information constitutes verification of outputs, key data (e.g. api tokens) etc. that are necessary for the success of the task, and agents could have obtained if they tried more or already obtained but failed to communicate to other agents before termination.

final_scope.name: Missing or incomplete verification
final_scope.rationale: The most frequently predicted category and a direct architectural omission: verification is optional in the observed workflows. A fixed execute-validate-decide skeleton maps cleanly onto Template Method.
final_scope.supporting_evidence: Model predictions: 26.6% of valid model responses (33.8% including rejected outputs), the highest of all categories. Human sample: 3/4 eligible human traces. Largest false-negative group against the upstream AI references (Step 7).
final_scope.contrary_evidence: Only 4 human traces are eligible, so human support is weak. No positive in the 17-case GitHub review. This sample does not establish how often verification failures occur.
final_scope.uncertainty: Predicted rates may partly reflect over-labelling; they are not human-verified prevalence.
final_scope.candidate_pattern: Template Method: execute, validate (task-specific hook), decide
final_scope.remediation_target: Make validation a required step before any result is accepted; reject an incorrect artifact with a reason.
final_scope.testable_claim: With a seeded incorrect artifact, the template version rejects it in every matched case where the baseline accepts it, without rejecting correct artifacts.

definitions.no_or_incomplete_verification: Lack of critical verification (system designed to but agents didn't) - - robustness (it covers also edge cases) - error handling etc. (broader) Failure to adequately validate or cross-check crucial information or decisions during the iterations, potentially leading to errors or vulnerabilities in the system. 1. verifier exists in the system, but it is weak or badly design 2. the system attempts to verify, but doesn't cover all aspects of the design to make a strong output This is implicitly True if 3.3 Lack of result verification is true, so no longer need to explicitly specify as True.

not_selected.disobey_task_specification: Strongest human signal (6/18 eligible human traces) and second-highest predicted rate, but a semantic failure that is hard to trigger on purpose and not tied to one structural pattern. Recorded as contrary evidence and a possible extension.
not_selected.fail_to_ask_for_clarification: 5/18 eligible human traces, but it needs ambiguous multi-agent exchanges and is hard to score objectively.
not_selected.loss_of_conversation_history: 2 team-reviewed GitHub positives (crewai-8219, crewai-8262) but little trace or model support. Kept as a handoff-contract requirement inside the T1 and T2 prototypes.
not_selected.conversation_reset: Human sample: 1/17 eligible human traces; one reviewed GitHub positive (langgraph-6064). It remains outside the agreed remediation scope; this added support is recorded for team review rather than silently changing scope.

notes: Samples are summarized separately and are not population prevalence estimates.
Model predictions are supporting evidence only, not human-verified labels.
